newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH POLL GIVES CENTRE-RIGHT REDUCED MAJORITY.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH POLL GIVES CENTRE-RIGHT REDUCED MAJORITY.

text.p: An opinion poll showed on Saturday that France's centre-right coalition could win a reduced but clear majority in a two-round parliamentary election on May 25 and June 1.

An IFOP poll, to be published on Sunday in the Journal du Dimanche, showed the governing coalition and conservative allies winning between 311 and 331 National Assembly seats, the Socialists between 200 and 220, Communists between 19 and 25, and the extreme-right National Front up to three seats.

The ruling coalition currently has 464 of the 577 seats. The poll, conducted on Friday, showed 23 percent of the 1,000-strong sample had not stated their voting intentions. President Jacques Chirac called the early election last Monday.

The projection was based on the following voting intentions: 37 percent for the centre-right RPR-UDF parties, 26 percent for the Socialists, 16 percent for the National Front, 10 percent for the Communist party, 6.5 percent for the ecologists, 2.5 percent for various right-wing parties and two percent for the extreme left.
The poll gives a total number of 555 seats for metropolitan France and excludes the 22 seats for overseas territories.

An IPSOS poll released last Thursday showed the centre-right winning only an eight-seat majority over the Socialists and Communists, rattling financial markets which view the left as less determined to pursue tough economic policies to bring France into the planned single European currency in 1999.
